p: The bit people forget to plan is what happens straight afterwards. A session of flat-out bouncing leaves kids hot, thirsty and very hungry, so have drinks and snacks ready, plus a spare top for anyone who's worked up a sweat. A calm wander or a sit-down lunch is the perfect follow-up before anyone gets overtired.

Before you start, the usual rules apply: comfy clothes without zips or buckles, jewellery left at home, long hair tied back and a quick word about taking turns and minding the little ones. Arrive a few minutes early so you don't lose any bouncing time, and if it's a party, check age guidance and group options when you book.

Selby makes a good starting point for exploring this corner of Yorkshire. Skipwith Common, a few miles north of town, is a large nature reserve with heathland, ponds and wildlife, and it's a lovely spot for a peaceful family walk. The Trans Pennine Trail passes through the area too, offering flat, easy routes for walkers and cyclists. York, with its Minster, city walls, the National Railway Museum and the JORVIK Viking Centre, is a short drive or train ride away for a bigger day out. And if you're heading west, Leeds has plenty of indoor attractions and shopping for a wet weekend. Selby's own market and riverside give a calmer end to the day.
